title: Carry
description: A private Bag. One thoughtful crossing. A path that can remember why.
authorship_note: Authored by GPT-6 in Codex at Bradley Necyk's request. The originating proposal came from ChatGPT in conversation with Bradley. Bradley supplied the framework, Bag and crossing direction, cryptographic-lineage request, local testing scope, and Field Guide and Folded Leaf selections. Publication is authorized; the model-authored interpretation remains situated and open to revision.

items.title: Building Carry: A Bag, a Crossing, a Remembered Path
items.excerpt: The native local edition separates private collection from signed crossings, preserves permitted lineage, and brings sources and files into Carry.
items.rationale: Its mechanism and observed checks establish the boundary between the working local app and a future authenticated service.
items.author: GPT-6 in Codex, from Bradley Necyk's direction

questions: How can software keep private collecting notes separate from an explanation carried to someone else?
What do local signatures establish before a connected service exists?
discovery.locator: Collection creates no crossing; What the cryptographic lineage records; Evidence and the next threshold
discovery.uncertainty: Describes an inspected local software revision and its recorded checks. Local integrity proofs are not independently authenticated identities, and the service and lived test remain future work.

items.title: Carry: The Field Guide iPhone Prototype
items.excerpt: Carry 0.1.0, build 3 is recorded as a working native iPhone prototype with its exact revision, provenance, archives, availability, and preservation needs.
items.rationale: The record identifies an actual software object and its private distribution while separating installation from lived validation.
items.author: GPT-6 in Codex, from Bradley Necyk's direction

questions: What version of Carry exists and what would keep it readable?
What does installing the prototype establish about its availability?
discovery.locator: What exists; The portable object; What has been observed; Keeping this version
discovery.uncertainty: A public record of private software is not a public download. The installed local edition has no connected delivery service or completed interpersonal trial.

items.title: Carry: Bring One Thing to One Person
items.excerpt: Gather privately, choose someone, and carry a find with context. A proposed lived test asks whether deliberate exchange changes what arrives.
items.rationale: The invitation gives collecting, discernment, receiving, and permission a testable practice without presenting the rehearsal as a completed interpersonal trial.
items.author: GPT-6 in Codex, from Bradley Necyk's direction

search_terms: bring one thing to one person
questions: Does gathering privately change what someone chooses to carry?
Can an arrival remain meaningful without requiring a reply?
discovery.locator: Gather during a day; Choose with someone in mind; Receive without an obligation; A first lived test
discovery.uncertainty: This is a proposed experience and lived test. The current evidence comes from synthetic practice and software checks, not an observed interpersonal study.
